chapter: Maple Leaf, own orchestra and rivals
title: Dance halls compared for sound; Economy Hall and Francs Amis
summary: Charles says Economy Hall was easiest to play; Francs Amis had a high ceiling that wore out the lip.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Tell him to come on in. Come on in. I wanted to ask you about the different halls and different places you played. Did some of them have a better sound than others? Why certainly. Well I figured that. Which one would sound the best, you know, make it easy to play?

Me I think Economy Hall was about the easiest one in the line of the colored folks, you understand? Now we play in many others. Licky Taze, Chans Ami, Prons Ami, you know, and many others. See? Just like those clubs. See?
But you know how some places are dead and it just wears your lip out? Oh yeah.
That Chans Ami was like that.
The ceiling was too high, you see? And you could just blow your brains out, you didn't get anything out of it.
Did you play upstairs or downstairs?
You always had upstairs. You know they had a music stand built upstairs.
You know they still got the whole- All those halls had music stands built upstairs. You know in the back?

They still got a hole in the ceiling there and I figured out what it was first to put the top of the string bass in. Up there on the balcony you'd have to stick the string bass up in there. Something else. See? And that was it. In the Chans Ami Hall. It was hard to blow with the high ceiling, huh? I see. That's just something I was curious about. What difference did it make, you know? What about Robichaud? Robichaud, did you play with him much?
